beats.say: It is two in the morning. You are not asleep. You are running the same conversation for the fortieth time. The one that has not happened yet.
beats.cap: It's 2 a.m. You're not asleep. You're running the same conversation for the 40th time. The one that hasn't happened yet.

lines.t: 2 A.M.
THE SAME CONVERSATION.
THE ONE THAT HAS NOT HAPPENED YET.

cues: It's 2 a.m.

The one that hasn't happened yet.

beats.say: That loop has a name in the oldest book most Indians own, and the book is not kind about it. It calls it grief for what has not happened. And it spends a whole chapter taking it apart.

ONE WHOLE CHAPTER.

beats.say: His limbs fail. His throat dries. His body trembles. The next verse adds that the bow slips from his hand. That is not cowardice. That is a body that has decided before the mind has.

scene.heading: BHAGAVAD GITA 1.29
sa: सीदन्ति मम गात्राणि मुखं च परिशुष्यति।
tr: sīdanti mama gātrāṇi mukhaṁ cha pariśhuṣhyati
vepathuśh cha śharīre me roma-harṣhaśh cha jāyate
scene.en: My limbs are failing me, my throat is parched, my body is trembling, and my hair is standing on end.
scene.author: Shri Purohit Swami
scene.src: BHAGAVAD GITA 1.29 · AFTER SHRI PUROHIT SWAMI, 1935 (EDITED TEXT)

cues: His limbs fail.

beats.say: Then he says the sentence the whole book hangs on. My mind is confused about my duty. Direct me. I am your disciple. Everything after this is an answer to that.
beats.cap: Then he says the sentence the whole book hangs on: My mind is confused about my duty. Direct me. I'm your disciple. Everything after this is an answer to that.

scene.heading: BHAGAVAD GITA 2.7
scene.en: My heart is oppressed with pity, and my mind is confused as to what my duty is. Therefore, my Lord, tell me what is best for my spiritual welfare, for I am Your disciple. Please direct me, I pray.
scene.author: Shri Purohit Swami
scene.src: BHAGAVAD GITA 2.7 · AFTER SHRI PUROHIT SWAMI, 1935 (EDITED TEXT)

cues: Then he says the sentence the whole book hangs on:

I'm your disciple.

beats.say: The first thing Krishna says is not comfort. It is a diagnosis. You are grieving for those who do not call for grief, and you sound wise while you do it. The wise, it says, grieve neither for the dead nor the living.
beats.cap: The first thing Krishna says isn't comfort. It's a diagnosis. You're grieving for those who don't call for grief, and you sound wise while you do it. The wise, it says, grieve neither for the dead nor the living.

scene.heading: BHAGAVAD GITA 2.11
scene.en: Lord Shri Krishna said: Why grieve for those for whom no grief is due, yet professing wisdom? The wise grieve neither for the dead nor the living.
scene.author: Shri Purohit Swami
scene.src: BHAGAVAD GITA 2.11 · AFTER SHRI PUROHIT SWAMI, 1935 (EDITED TEXT)

cues: The first thing Krishna says isn't comfort.

beats.say: Then the second move. Heat and cold, pleasure and pain, come from contact with the world. They come and they go. They are not permanent. Endure them.
beats.cap: Then the second move. Heat and cold, pleasure and pain, come from contact with the world. They come and they go. They aren't permanent. Endure them.

scene.heading: BHAGAVAD GITA 2.14
scene.en: Those external relations that bring cold and heat, pain and happiness come and go; they are not permanent. Endure them bravely, O Prince!
scene.author: Shri Purohit Swami
scene.src: BHAGAVAD GITA 2.14 · AFTER SHRI PUROHIT SWAMI, 1935 (EDITED TEXT)

beats.say: Our note. This is a weather model of feeling. A feeling is a front passing through, not a verdict on your life. The verse does not say the weather is not real. It says it moves.

IT IS REAL. AND IT MOVES.

beats.say: Now the part that reads like a case study. Two verses describe how a mind comes apart, one link at a time. It starts with dwelling on an object. Dwelling becomes attraction. Attraction becomes desire. Desire, blocked, becomes anger.
beats.cap: Now the part that reads like a case study. Two verses describe how a mind comes apart, one link at a time. It starts with dwelling on an object. Dwelling becomes attraction. Attraction becomes desire. Desire, blocked, becomes anger.

scene.heading: BHAGAVAD GITA 2.62
scene.en: When a person dwells on the objects of sense, they create an attraction for them; this attraction develops into desire, and desire breeds anger.
scene.author: Shri Purohit Swami
scene.src: BHAGAVAD GITA 2.62 · AFTER SHRI PUROHIT SWAMI, 1935 (EDITED TEXT)

cues: Now the part that reads like a case study.
Two verses describe how a mind comes apart, one link at a time.
It starts with dwelling on an object.
Dwelling becomes attraction.
Attraction becomes desire.
Desire, blocked, becomes anger.

beats.say: Anger brings delusion. Delusion wipes memory. Without memory, reason shatters. And when reason goes, the verse says, you are destroyed. Eight links. Every one of them familiar.
beats.cap: Anger brings delusion. Delusion wipes memory. Without memory, reason shatters. And when reason goes, the verse says, you're destroyed. Eight links. Every one of them familiar.

scene.heading: BHAGAVAD GITA 2.63
scene.en: Anger induces delusion; delusion leads to loss of memory; loss of memory results in the shattering of reason; and the destruction of reason leads to destruction.
scene.author: Shri Purohit Swami
scene.src: BHAGAVAD GITA 2.63 · AFTER SHRI PUROHIT SWAMI, 1935 (EDITED TEXT)

cues: Anger brings delusion.

beats.say: The Gita assumes a picture of the mind that an older text draws out in full. Picture a chariot. The body is the chariot. The intellect is the driver. The mind is the reins. The senses are the horses. The road is the things of the world. The self rides in it. When the mind lets go, the horses pull wherever they like.
beats.cap: The Gita assumes a picture of the mind that an older text draws out in full. Picture a chariot. The body is the chariot. The intellect is the driver. The mind is the reins. beats.say: Chapter two says the same thing with a boat. One straying sense the mind follows can carry the whole reason away, the way a storm tosses a ship at sea. Overthinking is the ship going sideways.
beats.cap: Chapter two says the same thing with a ship. One straying sense the mind follows can carry the whole reason away, the way a storm tosses a ship at sea. Overthinking is the ship going sideways.

scene.heading: BHAGAVAD GITA 2.67
tr: tadasya harati prajñāṁ vāyur nāvam ivāmbhasi
scene.en: As a ship at sea is tossed by the tempest, so the reason is carried away by the mind when preyed upon by straying senses.
scene.author: Shri Purohit Swami
scene.src: BHAGAVAD GITA 2.67 · AFTER SHRI PUROHIT SWAMI, 1935 (EDITED TEXT)

cues: Chapter two says the same thing with a ship.

beats.say: Here is the most quoted line in the book, and the most misquoted. You have the right to work, but never to the fruit of it. Do not make the fruit your motive. And do not use that as an excuse to do nothing.
beats.cap: Here's the most quoted line in the book, and the most misquoted. You have the right to work, but never to the fruit of it. Don't make the fruit your motive. And don't use that as an excuse to do nothing.

scene.heading: BHAGAVAD GITA 2.47
tr: mā karma-phala-hetur bhūr mā te saṅgo ’stvakarmaṇi
scene.en: But you have only the right to work, but none to the fruit of it. Let not the fruit of your action be your motive; nor be you enamored of inaction.
scene.author: Shri Purohit Swami
scene.src: BHAGAVAD GITA 2.47 · AFTER SHRI PUROHIT SWAMI, 1935 (EDITED TEXT)

cues: Here's the most quoted line in the book, and the most misquoted.
You have the right to work, but never to the fruit of it.

beats.say: Our note. Read it against the loop. Two in the morning is spent entirely on the fruit: the reply, the result, the verdict. The verse hands you back the only part that was ever yours: the next piece of work.

beats.say: The next verse gives the method a name. Act with the mind held steady, renounce attachment, look on success and failure with an equal eye. That equanimity, the verse says, is what yoga means; this translator's word for yoga is spirituality.

scene.heading: BHAGAVAD GITA 2.48
sa: योगस्थः कुरु कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा धनञ्जय।
सिद्ध्यसिद्ध्योः समो भूत्वा समत्वं योग उच्यते
tr: yoga-sthaḥ kuru karmāṇi saṅgaṁ tyaktvā dhanañjaya
siddhy-asiddhyoḥ samo bhūtvā samatvaṁ yoga uchyate
scene.en: Perform all your actions with your mind concentrated on the Divine, renouncing attachment and looking upon success and failure with an equal eye. Spirituality implies equanimity.
scene.author: Shri Purohit Swami
scene.src: BHAGAVAD GITA 2.48 · AFTER SHRI PUROHIT SWAMI, 1935 (EDITED TEXT)

cues: The next verse gives the method a name.

for yoga is spirituality.

beats.say: And two verses on, a definition that surprises people. The Sanskrit says yoga is skill in action; Purohit renders it as the true art of living. Either way: not withdrawal from action. Skill in it.
beats.cap: And two verses on, a definition that surprises people. The Sanskrit says yoga is skill in action; Purohit renders it as the true art of living. Either way: not withdrawal from action. Skill in it.

scene.heading: BHAGAVAD GITA 2.50
tr: tasmād yogāya yujyasva yogaḥ karmasu kauśhalam
scene.en: When a person attains Pure Reason, they renounce in this world the results of both good and evil. Cling to Right Action. Spirituality is the true art of living.
scene.author: Shri Purohit Swami
scene.src: BHAGAVAD GITA 2.50 · AFTER SHRI PUROHIT SWAMI, 1935 (EDITED TEXT)

cues: And two verses on, a definition that surprises people.
The Sanskrit says yoga is skill in action; Purohit renders it as the true art
of living.
Either way:

Skill in it.

beats.say: One more, because the loop always asks: what if I start and it goes wrong? On this path, the verse says, effort is never wasted. Even a little of it protects you from great danger.
beats.cap: One more, because the loop always asks: what if I start and it goes wrong? On this path, the verse says, effort is never wasted. Even a little of it protects you from great danger.

scene.heading: BHAGAVAD GITA 2.40
tr: svalpam apyasya dharmasya trāyate mahato bhayāt
scene.en: On this path, endeavour is never wasted nor repressed. Even a little practice of it protects one from great danger.
scene.author: Shri Purohit Swami
scene.src: BHAGAVAD GITA 2.40 · AFTER SHRI PUROHIT SWAMI, 1935 (EDITED TEXT)

beats.say: Arjuna asks what such a person is like. The answer ends with a picture. Rivers pour into the ocean from every side, and the ocean, brimming, remains the same. That is the mind the chapter is describing. Not empty. Full, and still.
beats.cap: Arjuna asks what such a person is like. The answer ends with a picture: rivers pour into the ocean from every side, and the ocean, brimming, remains the same. That's the mind the chapter is describing. Not empty. Full, and still.

scene.heading: BHAGAVAD GITA 2.70
scene.en: He attains peace into whom desires flow as rivers into the ocean, which, though brimming with water, remains ever the same; not he whom desires carry away.
scene.author: Shri Purohit Swami
scene.src: BHAGAVAD GITA 2.70 · AFTER SHRI PUROHIT SWAMI, 1935 (EDITED TEXT)

cues: Arjuna asks what such a person is like.

rivers pour into the ocean from every side, and the ocean, brimming,

Not empty.
Full, and still.

beats.say: Our note. Notice what the ocean does not do. It does not stop the rivers. Thoughts still arrive. The difference is that they arrive into something that does not rise and fall with each one.
beats.cap: Our note. Notice what the ocean does not do. It does not stop the rivers. Thoughts still arrive. The difference is that they arrive into something that does not rise and fall with each one.

lines.t: THE OCEAN DOES NOT STOP THE RIVERS.
IT DOES NOT RISE AND FALL WITH EACH ONE.

cues: Our note.
Notice what the ocean does not do.

beats.say: And a second picture, smaller. A tortoise drawing its limbs in. Not because the world is dangerous, but because it can. The ability to pull attention back is the skill the chapter is teaching.
beats.cap: And a second picture, smaller: a tortoise drawing its limbs in. Not because the world is dangerous, but because it can. The ability to pull attention back is the skill the chapter is teaching.

scene.heading: BHAGAVAD GITA 2.58
scene.en: He who can withdraw his senses from the attraction of their objects, as the tortoise draws its limbs within its shell—take it that such a one has attained perfection.
scene.author: Shri Purohit Swami
scene.src: BHAGAVAD GITA 2.58 · AFTER SHRI PUROHIT SWAMI, 1935 (EDITED TEXT)

cues: And a second picture, smaller:

beats.say: Here is the plain description, for the record. Unruffled in suffering. Not stirred by enjoyment. Without attachment, anger or fear. The chapter calls this a settled mind. Notice it never says a mind with nothing in it.
beats.cap: Here's the plain description, for the record: unruffled in suffering, not stirred by enjoyment, without attachment, anger or fear. The chapter calls this a settled mind. Notice it never says a mind with nothing in it.

scene.heading: BHAGAVAD GITA 2.56
scene.en: The sage whose mind is unruffled in suffering, whose desire is not aroused by enjoyment, who is without attachment, anger, or fear—take him to be one who stands at a lofty level.
scene.author: Shri Purohit Swami
scene.src: BHAGAVAD GITA 2.56 · AFTER SHRI PUROHIT SWAMI, 1935 (EDITED TEXT)

cues: Here's the plain description, for the record:
